title: dot11decrypt: AKM 18, 24, 25 and MLO support
description:
This patchset will revert and redo previous work. Also MLO decryption is implemented.

See commit message of https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22993/diffs?commit_id=afaf9a7a916c1f92e107b27b7490e5c0a1d95532 for rework reason.

commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Support decrypting MLO packets using TK
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Support decrypting MLO packets using TK

Decrypting unicast MLO traffic requires STA & AP MLD MAC address. Extend
current TK format to support it.
CCMP/GCMP AAD & Nonce building also changes.
Also add test case. The capture is from actual devices. The AP is
a Huawei BE3 Pro and the STA is a NCM865.

commits_data.title: dot11decrypt: Support AKM 18, 24, 25 with different PMK length
commits_data.message:
dot11decrypt: Support AKM 18, 24, 25 with different PMK length

Also add test cases. The added AKM 18(OWE) case covers 3 major DH groups
(group 19, 20, 21) thus it covers 3 PMK lengths.
Note that existing OWE case only covers group 19 but it tests GTK while
the newly added does not cover GTK. Keep the existing case.

commits_data.title: Revert "ieee80211: Add AKM 24 EAPOL decryption(dh group 19, 20, 21)"
commits_data.message:
Revert "ieee80211: Add AKM 24 EAPOL decryption(dh group 19, 20, 21)"

Previous work is incomplete and could have been implemented a lot better.

For AKM 18/24/25 with DH group 21, the PMK length is 64 bytes and this was
not supported.
Also PTK max length should be extented.

It's unnecessary to introduce new global state assoc_counter_in_auth for
getting MLD MAC address. Decrypting 4WHS relies on M1&M2 and since
MLD MAC addresses are provided in M1 and M2, there is no need to depend
on other packets. See [1].

Determining KCK/KEK/PTK size of AKM 18/24/25 using DH groups can be improved
by adopting the PMK size instead. Per IEEE 802.11, KCK/KEK/PTK length of such
AKMs is determined by hash algorithm used rather than the DH groups.
PMK length of such AKMs is the length of the hash algorithm's digest.
PMK is required to decrypt such 4WHS and PMK size is easily accessible
as the PMK is user-configured whereas acquiring the DH group depends on
capturing specific packets beforehand, an approach that is fragile.
Also more DH groups can be supported. See [2].
hostapd implements KCK/KEK/PTK size getter in the same way. See [3].

Reference:
[1] IEEE 802.11be-2024 12.7.6.1
[2] IEEE 802.11-2024 Table 12-11, 12.7.1.3, 12.14.2
[3] https://git.w1.fi/cgit/hostap/tree/src/common/wpa_common.c#n25

This reverts commit b6a98fc8263b0196411a36656047eb7371496bfc.
